text.p: Brian Lara unleashed a stunning display of hitting to power West Indies to a four-wicket victory over Australia in the World Series Cup on Sunday, eliminating the host team from the tournament.
West Indies overhauled Australia's 267 for seven with four balls of their 50 overs to spare, blasting 96 runs in the last 10 overs to silence a capacity crowd of about 25,000 at the WACA ground.
Lara bludgeoned three sixes and four fours in his innings of 90, bringing his total of runs in his last three Cup matches to 295.
The bulk of his runs came in an extraordinary last seven overs when his score jumped from 33 to 82 in the space of 24 balls.
Lara single-handedly turned the game around after West Indies had looked unlikely to catch Australia's total, scoring 16 off one over from leg-spinner Shane Warne which included two sixes.
At that stage West Indies needed to score at over nine an over and had just lost the crucial wicket of Carl Hooper for eight.

The victory for West Indies, their fifth in a row in the triangular competition, pushed them even further ahead at the top of the standings and eliminated Australia from the best-of-three finals later this month.
Pakistan are to be the other finalists.
Australia had not missed the finals of their annual World Series Cup since the inaugural competition in 1979-80 when West Indies triumphed, beating England in the finals.
Australia were given hope in the day-night game here after a battling 92 from opener Mark Waugh, with a late charge from middle-order batsmen Michael Bevan (35) and Greg Blewett (29).
Tight bowling from paceman Glenn McGrath and Warne in the middle overs appeared to tie down the West Indians, including Lara.
Lara took 61 balls to score his first 20 runs and no boundary was scored between the 17th and 34th overs.
But the late barrage from Lara sealed the result, earned him the man-of-the match award and confirmed him as the form batsman of the series.

The Trinidadian left-hander has enjoyed a remarkable change in fortune after failing to score more than 50 in his first 10 innings of this tour. His 90 followed an unbeaten 103 against Pakistan and 102 against Australia in his previous two Cup innings.
Lara's return to form must look ominous for the Australians, who have to face him again in the fourth test in Adelaide starting on January 25.
Australia lead the five-test series 2-1, but have lost their last five one-day matches and the third test. They have not won since December 8.
West Indies now travel to Sydney where they play Pakistan in a day-night match on Tuesday, a game with no bearing on qualifying for the finals.
